newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai Tyre & Rubber net surges, outlook good.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai Tyre & Rubber net surges, outlook good.

text.p: Shanghai Tyre and Rubber Co Ltd on Thursday announced a solid net profit for 1996, reversing a disastrous 1995 loss, largely due to falls in raw materials prices, analysts said.

"This is the turnaround story of the year, no doubt about it," said Bruce Richardson with HG Asia in Shanghai. "I think Tyre and Rubber is a harbinger of improved results for 1997 for B shares across the board."

The company's post-tax profit for 1996 was 109.128 million yuan, against a loss in 1995 of 170.51 million yuan under international accounting standards, the company reported in its annual results published on Thursday.
The company was helped by a string of good factors in the marketplace.
"The cost of rubber dropped by about 19 percent over the year, and their usage of rubber per tyre also declined," Richardson said. "Added to that, they had increased volume sales and higher prices."

The company's turnover rose to 3.98 billion yuan from 3.41 billion yuan based on domestic accounting standards, reflecting stronger sales as China continues its slow but steady transformation into a car culture.
"Sales in radial tyres, which are made for use on highways, climbed 200,000 to two million in 1996 with the opening of the Shanghai-Nanjing expressway," a local analyst said.

An analyst at a foreign brokerage in Shanghai said growing production of automobiles was helping to enlarge the market for Shanghai Tyre's products. Total vehicle production increased 1.5 percent in 1996 from 1995, official figures show.
After its poor showing in 1995, the company made a series of changes in top management in February last year, which analysts said had had a positive effect on performance.

"Good management is the guarantee of efficiency and quality," an analyst with one major local brokerage said. "I believe the company's 1997 outlook is optimistic now the improved management is in place."
Market conditions were likely to continue to go Shanghai Tyre's way in 1997 with rubber prices likely to fall further while sales were expected to continue to grow, analysts said.
One of the company's biggest customer, Shanghai Volkswagen Corp, has targeted a 10 percent increase in production in 1997.

"The prospects (for 1997) are pretty good," HG Asia's Richardson said. "I wouldn't want to put up a number, but management sees strong growth. They say they are aiming for 7.2 million tyre sales in 1997 compared with 6.8 million last year."
Tyre and Rubber's foreign currency B shares soared $0.052 or 9.96 percent to $0.574 on Thursday.
